method: mechanical inventory of the current /mlb render order, its sub-routes, and every shared component it imports; each row names an MLB owner, the NFL owner or gap, and the shared-vs-adapter decision. A row may be NOT_APPLICABLE only with a football-specific reason and a named replacement of equal user value.

statusVocabulary.SHIPPED: NFL has the capability through a named owner
statusVocabulary.ADOPTED_SHARED: NFL now consumes the same shared component MLB uses
statusVocabulary.ADAPTER_NEEDED: shared owner exists but its sport union/registry excludes nfl — additive extension required
statusVocabulary.NFL_OWNER_NEEDED: no shared owner exists; NFL needs its own component or route

rows.decision: STATED EXCLUSION — not the union widening P175 proposed. Widening SportKey in lib/normalize would force an entry into every exhaustive Record across Bank Builder, Moonshot, results and parlays for a sport that is definitionally excluded: churn on money surfaces with no reader benefit. What a reader needed was the REASON, and that is what shipped.
rows.note: the silent `continue` that made NFL's absence indistinguishable from an oversight is now a counted, reasoned refusal citing the same VALIDATED_PICK gate the money path enforces; a guard asserts the two answers cannot drift

The gate is now enforced in laneEligibility itself, fail-closed for unregistered sports, and a guard proves a VALIDATED_PICK leg WOULD qualify so the refusal is the gate and not a stub. Protected money hashes byte-identical

honesty: every row names an owner or an explicit gap — no row is hand-waved, and the two NOT_APPLICABLE rows each carry a football-specific reason and a named replacement of equal user value

0 rows are OPEN and 1 needs an adapter. This ledger exists so that count is visible rather than hidden behind the word 'complete' — it read 10 OPEN before P177, and this sentence is corrected with the count, never left to rot.

the cheapest real parity path is adopting owners that already exist and are sport-agnostic, not forking the /mlb page tree — 8 of the shared components MLB uses need no change at all, and 4 need only an additive registry/union entry
